fields.description: batter-outbound-http read_body (observed at 1630fe8d3f9b51b75417396bbd97478d4167b806, unchanged on master dd1ed7c1) accumulates response bytes in an ordinary Vec, grows it with reserve_exact, shrinks it with shrink_to_fit, drops partial bodies unwiped on size-limit failure, transport failure, cancellation, deadline expiry and exchange drop, and returns Body::Complete(Bytes::from(buffer)) with no zeroizing owner. Response bodies can carry bearer tokens and personal data, and a consumer cannot wipe partial buffers or allocations the transport has already released. Fix the storage this package owns; keep Body::Complete(Bytes), bounded buffering, modest initial allocation and all transport behaviour. Hyper, rustls and kernel buffers and independent caller copies stay out of scope.

Body::Complete(Bytes) is unchanged. Failure-path tests observe the wipe before deallocation with narrow test-only instrumentation and read no freed memory. Send-once, precedence, status retention, limits, exact bytes, redaction, labels and no new core/facade dependency are preserved. The guarantee and its exclusions are documented. Owning-guide checks and scripts/verify.sh are run and recorded with the platforms actually tested.
fields.title: Wipe outbound response-body storage before release

data.text: Design at 8853aa3c. Private ZeroizingBuffer (src/send/buffer.rs) owns one fixed Box<[u8]> at a time; its Drop zeroes the whole allocation, and with no reserve or shrink available, Drop is the only release path. Growth and the final fit build a replacement and assign over the old buffer. read_body keeps its growth policy, limit check, 1 MiB preallocation cap and select precedence. Body::Complete(Bytes) is preserved through Bytes::from_owner. Rejected: Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> (a reallocating Vec can release populated storage unwiped). Kept a protected final fit so a returned Bytes still retains exactly its length, as the old shrink_to_fit did; it copies only when capacity differs from length. Inspected resolved sources: bytes 1.12.1 owned vtable (last release drops the owner once; owned_is_unique is false; Vec/BytesMut conversion deep-copies) and zeroize 1.9.1 (volatile write per element). Public items are unchanged; zeroize is private and already in the normal graph through rustls; no Batter dependency added. ADR-010 review recorded in docs/evidence/api-assessments/http.md. Test instrumentation: cfg(test) probe called from the destructor between the wipe and deallocation, reading only live initialized memory. Ablations (Linux, focused lib tests): 13 of 13 protections removed one at a time were caught by the matching tests; restored tree passed. Release-build cost on Linux x86-64: zeroize 0.26 ms/1 MiB, 2.1 ms/8 MiB, 18 ms/64 MiB, synchronous on the releasing thread. Consumer note: Vec::from(bytes) was previously able to reclaim a unique allocation and now always copies, so a caller wrapping that Vec in its own zeroizing owner stays correct at the cost of one extra bounded copy.

Final commit 03076b228ecee20f6947e4f4e9d2c2ac4617438c, PR https://github.com/bpcakes/batter/pull/110. Supersedes the design note above on one point: the protected final fit was removed. A fresh independent review of 8853aa3c found no path that releases owned storage unwiped and no change to preserved transport behaviour, but showed the fit copies and wipes the whole body in the exchange's last poll, about 54 ms for a 60 MiB body by our own measurements, which can exceed RESERVE to reclaim less than half of an allocation. A completed body now keeps the allocation it grew into, at most twice its length and never above the limit (unit-tested). One growth step has the same synchronous cost, now disclosed in the deadline limits and on RESERVE: about 56 ms for 64 MiB. Review also corrected: a uniqueness claim tested only with a live clone (now tested on the sole handle), release-order wording (all six orders now executed), whole-allocation wording (tail dirtied so the wipe is distinguishable), a changelog line that understated the try_into_mut behaviour change, an architecture paragraph order and a hyper citation. Verification at this commit, Linux x86-64, rustc 1.98.1: cargo test -p batter-outbound-http --all-features --locked 116 passed; --no-default-features 103 passed; clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings clean; cargo doc --all-features --no-deps with -D warnings clean; bash scripts/verify.sh exit 0 (4616 passed, 0 failed, 436 ignored; formatting, file budgets, four Clippy configurations, six matrix parts, rustdoc, five HTTP smoke profiles). No ignored test is in this package. Ablations on this design: 13 of 13 protections removed one at a time failed the matching tests; restored tree passed. Limits: macOS has not run these tests, and hosted CI's macOS job compiles all targets but does not run this package's tests. The native Docker suites ran locally; the ignored external live suites did not. Hosted CI result to follow.
